clue.text: Bag of nuts

parts.note: nuts is slang for testicles, so the bag that holds them is the pouch of skin, not a sack of hazelnuts

explanation.surface: A shopping item: a sack of nuts from the greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a grocery bag; 'nuts' is the vulgar slang for testicles, Hoskins's trademark smut.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anatomical pouch of skin containing the testicles, slangily called nuts.

clue.text: Refurb Clio found in Settle and offer it for cash?

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: to settle or perch is to sit

indicators.note: a refurb is a do-over, so the letters of the car name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A refurbished Renault Clio, found in the town of Settle, being offered for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a Yorkshire market town; the 'it' offered for cash is sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer sexual services for money in public is the legal sense of soliciting.

clue.text: Dean erred badly, having smacked another on the tail

definitions.text: having smacked another on the tail

indicators.note: badly means the letters go wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dean made a mistake and spanked someone on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smacked' and 'tail' suggest a spanking; the definition means a car collision from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that hits the back of another vehicle has been in a rear collision.

clue.text: Express gratitude if leader of House cuts VAT

indicators.note: cuts means this letter slices into the other word

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The Leader of the House of Commons cutting value added tax would earn thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like value added tax; here it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To say you are grateful to someone is to show them gratitude in words.

clue.text: Teacher welcoming side-splitting form's misfortunes

indicators.note: welcoming means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: pupils call a female teacher Miss

indicators.note: side-splitting is read as having its sides split off, losing both end letters

parts.note: a form or outline is a shape

explanation.surface: A teacher welcoming a hilarious class's run of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-splitting' looks like 'hilarious'; read literally, the form has both its sides split off.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidents and unlucky events are misfortunes.

clue.text: Slavish type of tie with mum, bit of nuisance?

parts.note: a tie or link is a bond
mum, mother, is MA

indicators.note: a bit of the word nuisance is taken here as just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone tied to his mother's apron strings, a bit of a pest about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf or slave bound to serve a master is someone of slavish type.

clue.text: Fall for bishop free to express innermost homoerotism!

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, so a letter is pressed out of the word

parts.note: to free someone from a burden is to relieve them

indicators.note: innermost means the single central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bishop falling, freed to admit his secret homoerotic urges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innermost homoerotism' is the central R of the eleven-letter word, pressed out of RELIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall for a story is to be taken in by it, accepting it as true.

clue.text: It's a foregone conclusion I won't cheat on exam

parts.note: a refusal, I won't, is no
to cheat or swindle is to con
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student vowing honesty in an exam, sure of the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest with an obvious winner is a mismatch, its result a certainty.

clue.text: Flash old editor spoke like a sacred beast!

parts.note: a flash or moment is a mo

explanation.surface: An old editor talking in an instant like a holy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The sacred beast is the cow, venerated in Hinduism.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow lows, and the cow is sacred in Hinduism, so it speaks this way.

clue.text: Without any difficulties, lad turned up with feed

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a son
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: A boy who showed up for a meal and found it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual phrase saying a task gave no trouble at all.

clue.text: One known to spit lines with ace on a mike

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for an ace

indicators.note: on is read as tacked on to, so the letter for mike comes before the a it is attached to

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A rapper who spits lines into the mike, an ace performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like rap slang for delivering lines, but the definition means literal spitting, which camelids do.
explanation.definitionFit: South American camelids are notorious for spitting at anyone who annoys them.

clue.text: Prurient criminal is casual about love

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
criminal suggests something bent or corrupted, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dirty-minded crook treats romance in an offhand way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a lewd, unhealthy interest in sexual matters.

clue.text: Slow down partner or it's all over!

parts.note: to slow down or restrain something is to check it
a partner or friend is a mate

explanation.surface: A warning to a companion to brake before disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the winning move ends the game outright, so the term means total defeat.

clue.text: Dig German coming in with nothing on

indicators.note: coming in means one piece enters the middle of another

parts.note: with nothing on means naked, unclothed

explanation.surface: A German turning up naked at an archaeological dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig in the ribs is a poke with the elbow, a little push.

clue.text: Drinks round Mark returns and gives out

indicators.note: returns means the word for the mark is read backwards

parts.note: a round mark is a dot
something that gives out, fails or stops, dies

explanation.surface: A man called Mark buys a round, then comes back and hands them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks round' looks like a round of drinks; the definition is just 'Drinks' and 'round Mark' is a dot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot toddies are warming drinks of spirits, hot water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: Hoskins is the man out-of-head people mock

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself, Hoskins is becomes I'm
it, in a playground game, is the one who is 'it', the man

indicators.note: out-of-head means losing its first letter

parts.note: a people is a nation

explanation.surface: The setter boasts he is the man, while people out of their heads mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock article is a fake copy, made to look like the real thing.

clue.text: Ingenious English worker putting up stage

indicators.note: putting up means accommodating, so the stage is housed inside the other pieces

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
a stage of a journey is a leg

explanation.surface: A clever English labourer building a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenious solution is neat and simple, which is elegant in the mathematician's sense.

clue.text: Somehow other bran is loathsome

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bran of some other kind is disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome is repugnant, inspiring disgust.

clue.text: Strong wine compelled artist to hug one

indicators.note: to hug means the other letters close around this one

parts.note: if you were compelled to do something you were made to
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Strong drink forced a painter into embracing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name, so stronger than table wine.

clue.text: Dirty stuff Her Maj associates with society pals

parts.note: muck is dirt
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen mixing with dirty society friends.
explanation.walkthrough: MUCKERS is British slang for close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Muckers is British slang for close friends, people who muck in together.

clue.text: As behind, starts on numerous Indy crosswords

parts.note: a behind is the backside, British slang arse

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky comment that the Independent's crosswords are often rear-focused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word; it is the chemical symbol of the element.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for this poisonous element.

clue.text: Contrary article run by Times about revolutionary device

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so these two letters are reversed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: about means these letters sit around the revolutionary

parts.note: T stands for time, so times, plural, is TT
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a gadget printed by the Times, going against the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary device' looks like the definition, but 'revolutionary' is Che Guevara, the crossword's stock rebel; 'Contrary' reverses article and run, and 'about' wraps the times around him.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel with a pawl that allows turning in one direction only is a mechanical device.

clue.text: Nettles growing by the second! They're just over two feet!

indicators.note: the second here means the second letter of the word before

parts.note: the joints just above the feet are the ankles

explanation.surface: Nettles shooting up by the second, already standing above ankle height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettles' looks like the plant; it is the verb, annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, which is what a grievance does as it festers.

clue.text: Those making Her Maj's head spin can be idiots

definitions.text: Those making Her Maj's head spin
definitions.meaning: people who flip a coin set the monarch's head on it spinning
British slang insult for fools, jerks

explanation.surface: People who annoy the Queen are fools.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's head is on British coins, so coin-flippers send it spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin flippers spin the monarch's head; the same word is crude British slang for fools.

clue.text: Firm support for government committee

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a support garment

explanation.surface: A company lending backing to a government committee.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA (Cabinet Office Briefing Room A) is the UK government's emergency committee.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the British government's crisis response committee, after its meeting room.

clue.text: Britain loves Saint Nick, according to Americans

parts.note: love is zero, O, so loves is OO

explanation.surface: Britain adores Santa, says America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Nick' looks like Santa; 'Nick' is the definition, meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang to steal is to boost, as British slang uses nick.

clue.text: Fix to gatecrash functions or work picnics?

indicators.note: to gatecrash means to get inside, so this word enters the other

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function, so functions are sines
to fix or preserve meat is to cure it

explanation.surface: Arranging to crash parties or turning up uninvited to office picnics.
explanation.walkthrough: A picnic is also slang for an easy task, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushy posts needing little effort are, figuratively, picnics at work.

clue.text: Order endless Italian wine in empty café

indicators.note: in means the trimmed wine sits inside the other letters
empty means the word has its contents removed, leaving the outer letters
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: Asti is the sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Ordering Italian wine in a deserted café.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid social class or rank, as in the Hindu system, is an order.

clue.text: Massage oil on mate full of passion

indicators.note: to massage something is to knead and work it about, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Rubbing oil into a partner, which turns passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of passion is stirred by strong feelings.

clue.text: Panorama broadcast already taken in by viewers

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: something viewers have already taken in has been seen

explanation.surface: An episode of the BBC current affairs programme Panorama that viewers have already watched.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current affairs programme; here it is just a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide view, a sweeping outlook laid out before you.

clue.text: Wicked lookers a tan Icelander embraces

indicators.note: embraces means the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A sun-tanned Icelander hugging some good-looking people.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish and evil, as befits the devil himself.

clue.text: During deserted sessions, PM covers for members

indicators.note: during means this piece falls within the other
deserted means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: Edward Heath was the UK Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister covering for MPs during sparsely attended parliamentary sittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' looks parliamentary; it is the smutty sense, so the covers are condoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Condoms are rubber sheaths, covers for the male member.
